claims.text: The starting material consists of sub-10 nm equiatomic Au-Co-Cu-Ni-Pt nanoparticles.
The starting nanoparticles have a disordered solid-solution structure.
The sluggish-diffusion regime breaks down above 600 K.
Above the breakdown temperature, surface-energy-driven segregation dominates structural evolution.
Rapid vacancy-mediated diffusion occurs in the heated nanoparticles.
Heating is performed from room temperature to 1000 K at 15 °C/min with stabilization intervals.
The operating vacuum is approximately 10^-6 Pa.
Au has a higher vapor pressure than Co, Cu, Ni, and Pt under the stated conditions.
The high surface-to-volume ratio facilitates rapid surface diffusion and evaporation.
High surface energy in sub-10 nm particles lowers the activation barrier for surface diffusion.
Au segregates to the particle surface and evaporates preferentially.
The remaining particle core rapidly phase-separates and becomes Au-depleted.
High-temperature exposure can cause selective elemental depletion and mass loss in high-entropy alloys despite proposed entropy or sluggish-diffusion effects.
Preferential Au loss causes reduction in particle size and disappearance of the smallest particles.
The particles evolve from spherical to faceted or irregular shapes because of anisotropic surface-energy minimization.
A stable single-phase solid solution will not be present at 1000 K.
High configurational entropy and sluggish diffusion are theoretically expected to preserve a single-phase solid solution and prevent phase separation up to 1000 K.
Surface effects dominate specifically below 10 nm, whereas particles larger than 50 nm are governed more strongly by bulk diffusion and entropy stabilization.
The precise transition temperature cannot be established without directly measuring diffusion coefficients in Au-Co-Cu-Ni-Pt nanoparticles.
Combined in situ HTXRD, TEM, species-resolved QMS, and surface-composition analysis can test phase retention, shape evolution, elemental loss, and surface segregation during heating.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis specifies a breakdown threshold above 600 K, while the uncertainty field states that the specific transition temperature is unknown without direct diffusion measurements.
